shared: Base: the code as on master, including MAX_CRITERIA and tooBig() in src/slopify/workflows/shape.ts. Single-card shape (no `split` arg) keeps its behavior, its result types, its writer schema, and its tests unchanged.

Split mode is a mode of the `shape` workflow, selected by the arg `split: true`. Args: `{idea: string (the request), split: true, cap?: number | numeric string, projectRoot?: string}`. Before any dispatch, run() returns `{status: 'not-started', next}` when split is set with `card`, with `kind` other than story, without `idea`, or with a `cap` that is present but not a whole number of 1 or more. The `next` text says what to fix.

The cap: the `cap` arg when given; otherwise min(statedCap > 0 ? statedCap : MAX_CARDS, MAX_CARDS), with MAX_CARDS = 20 and statedCap read by the planner. A cap read from the request can lower the limit, never raise it. Covered parts never count against the cap.

src/slopify/lib/split.ts (new) exports, used by shape.ts exactly as stated: `MAX_CARDS`; `PLAN_SCHEMA` = {constraints: string[], statedCap: integer (0 when the request states none), parts: [{key: string, outcome: string, dependsOn: string[] (keys)}], omitted: [{part: string, reason: string}]}, all fields required; `type Plan = Infer<typeof PLAN_SCHEMA>`; `interface Part { id: string; key: string; outcome: string; dependsOn: string[] }`, where `id` is the planner key sanitized with slugOf and prefixed with its zero-padded plan index, unique in the run, and `dependsOn` holds ids; `capArgOf(arg: unknown): number | null | 'invalid'` (null when absent); `capOf(argCap: number | null, statedCap: number): number`; `partsOf(plan: Plan): { parts: Part[]; dropped: string[] }` (renames duplicate keys, drops dependsOn keys that name no part and describes each drop in `dropped`); `orderParts(parts: readonly Part[]): Part[]` (flattened waves() from lib/rules.ts with `files: []`, so every dependency precedes its dependent, and a cycle or unknown id falls back to plan order); `selectParts(ordered: readonly Part[], covered: ReadonlySet<string>, cap: number): { selected: Part[]; overCap: Part[] }` (the first `cap` uncovered parts in order); `REQUIRED_PARTS: readonly string[]` (the story template's required part names); `missingParts(reported: readonly { name: string; words: number }[]): string[]` (each required part absent or with 0 words); `checkedId(id: string, locations: readonly string[]): string` (the trimmed id when it is one token and equals one of the locations, else ''); `splitReport(r: { cards: SplitCard[]; covered: Covered[]; leftOut: LeftOut[]; dropped: string[]; unrelated: string[] }): string`.

Result types (shape.ts): `interface SplitCard { part: string; card: string; deliverable: boolean; openQuestions: string[] }`, `interface Covered { part: string; card: string }`, `interface LeftOut { part: string; reason: string }` (exported from split.ts for splitReport); `interface Split { status: 'done'; workflow: 'shape'; cards: SplitCard[]; covered: Covered[]; leftOut: LeftOut[]; report: string }`. run() returns `Promise<NotStarted | Stopped | Shaped | Duplicate | Split>`. `part` is always the Part id.

The report names every part of the plan exactly once: filed (with card id and whether it is Deliverable, plus its open questions), already covered by <card>, or left out with its reason. Left-out reasons: each planner `omitted` entry with its reason; `over the cap of N`; `still missing <parts> after the revisions`. It also lists each dropped plan edge and each dependency relation not recorded because the part it depends on got no card.

Hidden line of a split card: markerOf(`${slugged(request)} ${slugged(part key)}`) using shape.ts's existing markerOf, so two requests with the same part key never share a line. A rerun finds an earlier run's card for a part by this line.

A model-chosen id (advisor-fit duplicateOf or overlaps) counts only after checkedId against the locations of that part's scout-related-cards evidence; an id that fails is dropped and named in the run's log. Relation targets are checked ids, covering-card ids, or ids this run's pusher returned.

Pusher brief for a split card names exactly one create and no update to any existing card: `The user's invocation of shape with this request authorizes filing at most N cards; this is one of them: create one card from the draft below, as docs/BOARD.md declares, set its Shaped and Deliverable labels as asked, and record the relations named below. Nothing else: no commit, branch, push, PR, other card, or change to an existing card.` It adds `Record that the card is blocked by <ids>.` when it has blocking ids and `Record that the card is related to <ids>.` when it has related ids, each through docs/BOARD.md's relation binding. Labels and the hidden-line handling follow single mode's file().

The relation binding on a board is append-only `blockedBy`, `blocks`, `relatedTo` on Create and on Update. A relation the project does not bind is reported unmet by pusher, never improvised, and ends the run as H2 through pushed().

Planner agent `slopify:writer-split`: a producer that writes no file and touches no board; it returns PLAN_SCHEMA from the request and the shared grounding evidence. Its prompt carries the cap and the request fenced.
In split mode, writer-card's dispatch also returns `parts: [{name: string, words: integer}]`, each template part the draft holds with its word count. Single mode's WRITER_SCHEMA stays as it is.

tasks.todo: Add split mode to shape.ts. Input: the shared arg checks, all before createDeliver dispatches anything. Flow: (1) Read and Ground once for the request: one related-cards search and one ground() whose evidence every part shares. (2) Plan: one writer-split dispatch returning PLAN_SCHEMA (a null result halts as today through must()); partsOf, then orderParts; the cap from capOf. (3) Coverage for every part, in bounded waves of about 5 run with parallel(): a scout-related-cards search for the part that asks for the part's hidden line; a card holding that line covers the part; otherwise adviseAll on the shared evidence plus the part's related cards, where a checked duplicateOf covers the part and checked overlaps become relatedTo targets. FIT_SCHEMA in family.ts gains `overlaps` as an optional STRINGS property, not in `required`, so single mode and its stubs are unaffected. A covered card is never updated or marked a duplicate. (4) selectParts: only the selected parts are drafted; over-cap parts go to leftOut with `over the cap of N`. (5) Draft and refine the selected parts in bounded waves: each part's Card has kind story, its idea is the part's outcome, then every planner constraint listed under a line saying it applies to every card in the set, then the request fenced; its draft path is under `.tmp/shape/<slugged(request)>/<part id>.md`; write and refine reuse the existing write/checkDraft/rule/refine path with the advisor views from step 3 (no second advise or ground), and in split mode the writer also returns `parts` and refine adds missingParts as a counted problem beside tooBig. A part whose last revision still misses a required part is not filed and goes to leftOut with `still missing <parts> after the revisions`. (6) File sequentially in order: before each pusher dispatch add one to an attempts counter and never dispatch when attempts would exceed the cap, so a create whose read-back fails still uses a slot; the brief is the shared split pusher brief; blockedBy is the filed or covering card of each dependency (a dependency with no card records nothing and goes to the report's unrelated list); deliverable is no open question, as single mode; record each filed card with d.done(`card <id> for <part id>`). Waves: parallel() turns a throw into null, so each part's work is wrapped to keep the first Halt and rethrow it after the wave, the way changeHoldingHalt does in loop.ts, so stopOf still returns Stopped with the cards already filed; a shared helper may be extracted from loop.ts for this. Return Split with splitReport. meta: whenToUse documents `split` and `cap` (split: true with the request as idea breaks it into up to cap story cards, 20 when not given; pass a cap the user states as `cap`), and phases gain `Plan`. Rebuild plugins/slopify/workflows/shape.js. Fake board (test/linear-board.ts): each card stores blockedBy and relatedTo ids parsed from the brief's `blocked by`/`related to` sentences, and clearBoard resets them. Tests in test/shape-split.test.ts with stubbed agents, one per Deterministic criterion: cap N with N+2 parts gives exactly N pusher create dispatches (and a pusher reporting done:false still uses a slot); every filed card's writer reply reports every required part with words > 0 and a part that never reports `Out of scope` is not filed and is named; part b depends on part a and b's card on the fake board holds exactly a's id in blockedBy (pusher returns a fresh id per call); a planner `omitted` part and an over-cap part are named in the report; a fake-board card holding a part (by advisor-fit duplicateOf found in that part's related evidence, and by an earlier run's hidden line) gets no card and the report names it; a rerun on the same request leaves the board size unchanged. Robustness tests: two requests sharing a part key each file their card; a stated cap of 50 with no arg files at most 20; an invalid cap or split with card returns not-started with no dispatch; a duplicateOf id absent from the part's scout evidence is not treated as covering; every per-part writer-card brief contains every planner constraint; a pusher reporting unmet on the second card returns Stopped naming the first card in completed, and a rerun files only the missing card. Existing shape tests keep passing unchanged except where a stub needs the new optional field.

decisions.question: New workflow or a mode of shape?
decisions.choice: A mode of shape, selected by `split: true` with the request as `idea`.
decisions.rationale: SMR-358 fixed the set of workflows and the issue allows a mode; every per-card step already exists in shape.ts.

decisions.question: Where does the cap come from, and can the model raise it?
decisions.choice: The `cap` arg when given, else min(stated cap or 20, 20); an invalid present cap returns not-started before any dispatch.
decisions.rationale: The issue makes the request the authorization up to the cap; a model-read cap may lower it but never raise it.

decisions.question: When is the cap applied, and what does it count?
decisions.choice: Applied before drafting to uncovered parts in dependency order; at filing, attempts are counted before each pusher dispatch.
decisions.rationale: No tokens spent on cards that can't be filed, and a create with a failed read-back still uses a slot, so N is never exceeded.

decisions.question: How is a part already covered by a board card found?
decisions.choice: First an exact request-plus-part hidden line; else advisor-fit duplicateOf, accepted only when the id is in that part's scout-related-cards evidence.
decisions.rationale: The line makes reruns of the same request exact; advisor-fit covers hand-filed cards; the location check stops an invented id.

decisions.question: How is a dependency recorded?
decisions.choice: blockedBy on the dependent card's create, naming the filed or covering card of each dependency; relatedTo for partial overlaps; bound on Create and Update in docs/BOARD.md.
decisions.rationale: Linear's save_issue schema accepts append-only blockedBy/relatedTo; the issue asks the delivery to confirm before building on it, which is left as a manual action.

decisions.question: How is 'every required template part, none empty' guaranteed?
decisions.choice: In split mode writer-card reports parts with word counts; a counted missingParts problem goes back to the writer; a part still missing after the last revision is not filed and is reported.
decisions.rationale: A code gate, in the tooBig pattern, rather than a model's word alone; single mode stays as it is.

decisions.question: How do whole-set constraints reach every card?
decisions.choice: Code appends every planner constraint to every part's idea.
decisions.rationale: The Full eval criterion depends on all three constraints on every card; leaving it to each writer would lose some.

decisions.question: Parallel or sequential parts, and what happens to a halt?
decisions.choice: Coverage and drafting in bounded parallel waves, holding the first Halt and rethrowing after the wave; filing sequential in order.
decisions.rationale: parallel() turns a throw into null; Halt has no kind, so a budget or binding halt must end the run rather than repeat per part.

decisions.question: Who plans the split?
decisions.choice: A new producer agent writer-split that returns PLAN_SCHEMA and writes no file.
decisions.rationale: Keeps writer-card's single role and avoids a plan file nothing reads; plugin-code wants consumed output in typed fields.

decisions.question: What identifier pattern does checkedId accept?
decisions.choice: One token with no whitespace that equals a location in the part's scout-related-cards evidence.
decisions.rationale: The plugin names no tracker, so it can't hard-code a board's identifier format; matching the scout's own locations is the real guard.

decisions.question: Does a rerun repair relations on cards it did not file?
decisions.choice: No. A split run never updates an existing card, including covered ones.
decisions.rationale: The issue authorizes filing up to the cap and nothing more.
